experiments.name: dependent chain
experiments.asm: fsqrt.s $f0, $f0; fsqrt.s $f0, $f0; movfr2gr.s $r4, $f0; and $r4, $r4, $r5; or $r4, $r4, $r6; movgr2fr.w $f0, $r4
experiments.command: ./bench --unroll 2000 --iters 300 --warmup 10 --reps 7 --core 0 --init 'li.d $r4, 1065353216; movgr2fr.w $f0, $r4; li.d $r5, -1; li.d $r6, 0' --asm 'fsqrt.s $f0, $f0; fsqrt.s $f0, $f0; movfr2gr.s $r4, $f0; and $r4, $r4, $r5; or $r4, $r4, $r6; movgr2fr.w $f0, $r4'

latencies.notes: Data-dependent latency: 8 cycles for 0/Inf/NaN/negative; 10 for exact squares 1, 4, 0.25 and minnorm; 22 for general non-square inputs; 23 for maxsub and minsub. Measured with an integer-bit reset chain; 5 cycles of helper latency are subtracted. The sample experiment uses 1.0.

throughput.notes: Data-dependent throughput: CPI 4.5 for special values; 5.5 for exact squares; 11.5 for general inputs; 12.0 for maxsub and minsub. Throughput is initiation-interval bound.

notes: Latency model, fitted and validated on this core with a two-copy chain (the stored experiment runs the operation twice, subtracts the 6-cycle closure and divides by 2). Classes: 8 cycles for special operands (0, Inf, NaN), 10 cycles for the exact / power-of-two path (the stored sample uses 1.0), 22 cycles for a general operand. For 32-bit lanes the vector latency equals 2 x the scalar latency - 5, because the 32-bit lanes make two passes over the 64-bit datapath and share the setup/rounding. 64-bit vector lanes match the scalar numbers exactly and run in parallel, only the slowest lane matters.
